description: .NET client for Chroma and Chroma Cloud, tested with Chroma 0.4.10 to 1.5.9. Community project, not affiliated with Chroma.
releaseNotes: 2.9.0: the settings of a new collection: the HNSW index (ChromaHnswConfiguration), the SPANN index of Chroma Cloud (ChromaSpannConfiguration) and the embedding function it declares; the indexes of the values in a schema, WithIndex and WithoutIndex; on Chroma Cloud, MaxScore sparse indexes and a customer-managed key, WithGcpCmek; the embedding function in ModifyConfigurationAsync; ChromaCollection.Dimension, Version and LogPosition; doubles and floats written with the fewest digits that read back as them, whole ones as floats, and read right on .NET Framework; the integer HNSW settings of the metadata, like hnsw:construction_ef, as integers; an ArgumentException before the request for what a server would store changed or drop: lone surrogates, ulongs above long.MaxValue, empty lists in the metadata of records, lists in the metadata of collections, names that the path of a URL drops, an HNSW index with fewer than 2 neighbors; the netstandard2.0 build takes the 8.0 packages, with no warnings on .NET 6 and 7; the package icon and the vector-database tag. 2.8.0: the BM25 vectors computed from the schema and text queries in SparseKnn, as the Python client of Chroma does; the space of a collection with a schema; writes in batches and reads in pages by default, 300 records at a time on Chroma Cloud, and the quota a rejection tells; traces and metrics with OpenTelemetry (ChromaTelemetry); ChromaConfigurationOptions.FromConnectionString; clients that tests can mock; ids in QueryAsync; ChromaEmbeddingFunctionReference.Known, for the other functions of a schema; a .NET Framework 4.6.2 build, which runs next to OpenTelemetry without binding redirects; every parameter and result documented. The API follows the .NET conventions, the Async suffix and read-only lists among them: how to adapt in https://github.com/ChromaDotNet/ChromaDB.Client/releases/tag/v2.8.0. 2.7.1: the description of the package says that it is a community project, not affiliated with Chroma, and the tags have chroma-cloud. 2.7.0: for Chroma Cloud, the Search API: ChromaCollectionClient.Search with ChromaSearch, ChromaRank (Knn, SparseKnn, Rrf and the arithmetic of ranks) and ChromaSearchGroupBy; sparse vectors in metadata, ChromaSparseVector, and the schema of a collection with sparse vector indexes, ChromaCollectionSchema and ChromaCollection.SparseVectorIndexes; ChromaBm25, the BM25 function of Chroma, with the same vectors as its Python client; Add, Update and Upsert compute the BM25 vectors that the schema declares, and SparseKnn takes a text, as the Python client does; new ChromaClient(uri) and new ChromaClient(options), with an HttpClient of their own that Dispose closes. 2.6.0: the rest of the v2 API: ChromaWhereDocumentOperator.Regex and NotRegex; Delete(ChromaDelete) by filters, with a limit and the count of the deleted records; ModifyConfiguration, for the settings of the index of the collection; Healthcheck; Count(ChromaReadLevel); ChromaClient.WithTenantAndDatabaseFromIdentity; for Chroma Cloud Fork, ForkCount, GetIndexingStatus, AttachFunction, GetAttachedFunction, DetachFunction, GetCollectionByCrn and UpdateTenant. XML documentation in the package. Fixed: ChromaCollection.Space also reads the space that Chroma Cloud sends in the spann configuration; the validation errors of the 0.x servers are the message of the exception. 2.5.0: embeddings in base64 where the server declares supports_base64_encoding; WithBatchSplitting(maxBatchSize) for servers like Chroma Cloud, which declares 1000 but takes 300 records per write; ChromaException.ErrorType; CollectionExists also by a NotFoundError about a collection. 2.4.1: works in applications published with trimming or NativeAOT: serialization with metadata generated at build time, IsAotCompatible. All the releases: https://github.com/ChromaDotNet/ChromaDB.Client/releases. Tested versions: https://github.com/ChromaDotNet/ChromaDB.Client/blob/main/docs/COMPATIBILITY.md. Migration from 1.x: https://github.com/ChromaDotNet/ChromaDB.Client#migrating-from-chromadbclient-1x
